member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_COMMAND
member.summary: Sent when the user selects a command item from a menu, when a control sends a notification message to its parent window, or when an accelerator keystroke is translated.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_COMMNOTIFY
member.summary: Represents the common action is performed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_COMPACTING
member.summary: Sent to all top-level windows when the system detects more than 12.5 percent of system time over a 30- to 60-second interval is being spent compacting memory. This indicates that system memory is low.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_COMPAREITEM
member.summary: Sent to determine the relative position of a new item in the sorted list of an owner-drawn combo box or list box. Whenever the application adds a new item, the system sends this message to the owner of a combo box or list box created with the CBS_SORT or LBS_SORT style.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CONTEXTMENU
member.summary: Notifies a window that the user clicked the right mouse button (right-clicked) in the window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_COPY
member.summary: An application sends the WM_COPY message to an edit control or combo box to copy the current selection to the clipboard in CF_TEXT format.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_COPYDATA
member.summary: An application sends the WM_COPYDATA message to pass data to another application.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CREATE
member.summary: Sent when an application requests that a window be created by calling the CreateWindowEx or CreateWindow function. (The message is sent before the function returns.) The window procedure of the new window receives this message after the window is created, but before the window becomes visible.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CTLCOLORBTN
member.summary: The WM_CTLCOLORBTN message is sent to the parent window of a button before drawing the button. The parent window can change the button's text and background colors. However, only owner-drawn buttons respond to the parent window processing this message.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CTLCOLORDLG
member.summary: Sent to a dialog box before the system draws the dialog box. By responding to this message, the dialog box can set its text and background colors using the specified display device context handle.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CTLCOLOREDIT
member.summary: An edit control that is not read-only or disabled sends the WM_CTLCOLOREDIT message to its parent window when the control is about to be drawn. By responding to this message, the parent window can use the specified device context handle to set the text and background colors of the edit control.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CTLCOLORLISTBOX
member.summary: Sent to the parent window of a list box before the system draws the list box. By responding to this message, the parent window can set the text and background colors of the list box by using the specified display device context handle.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CTLCOLORMSGBOX
member.summary: Send to owner window before draws the MessageBox.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CTLCOLORSTATIC
member.summary: A static control, or an edit control that is read-only or disabled, sends the WM_CTLCOLORSTATIC message to its parent window when the control is about to be drawn. By responding to this message, the parent window can use the specified device context handle to set the text foreground and background colors of the static control.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_CUT
member.summary: An application sends a WM_CUT message to an edit control or combo box to delete (cut) the current selection, if any, in the edit control and copy the deleted text to the clipboard in CF_TEXT format.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_ACK
member.summary: The WM_DDE_ACK message notifies a Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) application of the receipt and processing of the following messages: WM_DDE_POKE, WM_DDE_EXECUTE, WM_DDE_DATA, WM_DDE_ADVISE, WM_DDE_UNADVISE, WM_DDE_INITIATE, or WM_DDE_REQUEST (in some cases).

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_ADVISE
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) client application posts the WM_DDE_ADVISE message to a DDE server application to request the server to supply an update for a data item whenever the item changes. To post this message, call the PostMessage function with the following parameters.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_DATA
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) server application posts a WM_DDE_DATA message to a DDE client application to pass a data item to the client or to notify the client of the availability of a data item.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_EXECUTE
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) client application posts a WM_DDE_EXECUTE message to a DDE server application to send a string to the server to be processed as a series of commands. The server application is expected to post a WM_DDE_ACK message in response.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_FIRST
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) client application posts a WM_DDE_FIRST message to a DDE server application to send a string to the server to be processed as a series of commands. The server application is expected to post a WM_DDE_ACK message in response.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_INITIATE
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) client application sends a WM_DDE_INITIATE message to initiate a conversation with a server application responding to the specified application and topic names. Upon receiving this message, all server applications with names that match the specified application and that support the specified topic are expected to acknowledge it.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_LAST
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) client application posts a WM_DDE_LAST message to a DDE server application.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_POKE
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) client application posts a WM_DDE_POKE message to a DDE server application. A client uses this message to request the server to accept an unsolicited data item. The server is expected to reply with a WM_DDE_ACK message indicating whether it accepted the data item.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_REQUEST
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) client application posts a WM_DDE_REQUEST message to a DDE server application to request the value of a data item.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_TERMINATE
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) application (client or server) posts a WM_DDE_TERMINATE message to terminate a conversation.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DDE_UNADVISE
member.summary: A Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) client application posts a WM_DDE_UNADVISE message to inform a DDE server application that the specified item or a particular clipboard format for the item should no longer be updated. This terminates the warm or hot data link for the specified item.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DEADCHAR
member.summary: Posted to the window with the keyboard focus when a WM_KEYUP message is translated by the TranslateMessage function. WM_DEADCHAR specifies a character code generated by a dead key. A dead key is a key that generates a character, such as the umlaut (double-dot), that is combined with another character to form a composite character. For example, the umlaut-O character (Ö) is generated by typing the dead key for the umlaut character, and then typing the O key.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DELETEITEM
member.summary: Sent to the owner of a list box or combo box when the list box or combo box is destroyed or when items are removed by the LB_DELETESTRING, LB_RESETCONTENT, CB_DELETESTRING, or CB_RESETCONTENT message. The system sends a WM_DELETEITEM message for each deleted item. The system sends the WM_DELETEITEM message for any deleted list box or combo box item with nonzero item data.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DESTROY
member.summary: Sent when a window is being destroyed. It is sent to the window procedure of the window being destroyed after the window is removed from the screen. This message is sent first to the window being destroyed and then to the child windows (if any) as they are destroyed. During the processing of the message, it can be assumed that all child windows still exist.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DESTROYCLIPBOARD
member.summary: Sent to the clipboard owner when a call to the EmptyClipboard function empties the clipboard.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DEVICECHANGE
member.summary: Notifies an application of a change to the hardware configuration of a device or the computer.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DEVMODECHANGE
member.summary: The WM_DEVMODECHANGE message is sent to all top-level windows whenever the user changes device-mode settings.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DISPLAYCHANGE
member.summary: The WM_DISPLAYCHANGE message is sent to all windows when the display resolution has changed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DRAWCLIPBOARD
member.summary: Sent to the first window in the clipboard viewer chain when the content of the clipboard changes. This enables a clipboard viewer window to display the new content of the clipboard.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DRAWITEM
member.summary: Sent to the parent window of an owner-drawn button, combo box, list box, or menu when a visual aspect of the button, combo box, list box, or menu has changed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_DROPFILES
member.summary: Sent when the user drops a file on the window of an application that has registered itself as a recipient of dropped files.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_ENABLE
member.summary: Sent when an application changes the enabled state of a window. It is sent to the window whose enabled state is changing. This message is sent before the EnableWindow function returns, but after the enabled state (WS_DISABLED style bit) of the window has changed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_ENDSESSION
member.summary: The WM_ENDSESSION message is sent to an application after the system processes the results of the WM_QUERYENDSESSION message. The WM_ENDSESSION message informs the application whether the session is ending.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_ENTERIDLE
member.summary: Sent to the owner window of a modal dialog box or menu that is entering an idle state. A modal dialog box or menu enters an idle state when no messages are waiting in its queue after it has processed one or more previous messages.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_ENTERMENULOOP
member.summary: Notifies an application's main window procedure that a menu modal loop has been entered.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE
member.summary: Sent one time to a window after it enters the moving or sizing modal loop. The window enters the moving or sizing modal loop when the user clicks the window's title bar or sizing border, or when the window passes the WM_SYSCOMMAND message to the DefWindowProc function and the wParam parameter of the message specifies the SC_MOVE or SC_SIZE value. The operation is complete when DefWindowProc returns. The system sends the WM_ENTERSIZEMOVE message regardless of whether the dragging of full windows is enabled.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_ERASEBKGND
member.summary: Sent when the window background must be erased (for example, when a window is resized). The message is sent to prepare an invalidated portion of a window for painting.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_EXITMENULOOP
member.summary: Notifies an application's main window procedure that a menu modal loop has been exited.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_EXITSIZEMOVE
member.summary: Sent one time to a window, after it has exited the moving or sizing modal loop. The window enters the moving or sizing modal loop when the user clicks the window's title bar or sizing border, or when the window passes the WM_SYSCOMMAND message to the DefWindowProc function and the wParam parameter of the message specifies the SC_MOVE or SC_SIZE value. The operation is complete when DefWindowProc returns.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_FONTCHANGE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_FONTCHANGE message to all top-level windows in the system after changing the pool of font resources.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_GETDLGCODE
member.summary: Sent to the window procedure associated with a control. By default, the system handles all keyboard input to the control; the system interprets certain types of keyboard input as dialog box navigation keys. To override this default behavior, the control can respond to the WM_GETDLGCODE message to indicate the types of input it wants to process itself.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_GETFONT
member.summary: Retrieves the font with which the control is currently drawing its text.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_GETHOTKEY
member.summary: Sent to determine the hot key associated with a window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_GETICON
member.summary: Sent to a window to retrieve a handle to the large or small icon associated with a window. The system displays the large icon in the ALT+TAB dialog, and the small icon in the window caption.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_GETMINMAXINFO
member.summary: Sent to a window when the size or position of the window is about to change. An application can use this message to override the window's default maximized size and position, or its default minimum or maximum tracking size.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_GETOBJECT
member.summary: Sent by both Microsoft Active Accessibility and Microsoft UI Automation to obtain information about an accessible object contained in a server application.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_GETTEXT
member.summary: Copies the text that corresponds to a window into a buffer provided by the caller.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_GETTEXTLENGTH
member.summary: Determines the length, in characters, of the text associated with a window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_HANDHELDFIRST
member.summary: Represents the window message that handled first.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_HANDHELDLAST
member.summary: Represents the window message that handled last.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_HELP
member.summary: Indicates that the user pressed the F1 key. If a menu is active when F1 is pressed, WM_HELP is sent to the window associated with the menu; otherwise, WM_HELP is sent to the window that has the keyboard focus. If no window has the keyboard focus, WM_HELP is sent to the currently active window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_HOTKEY
member.summary: Posted when the user presses a hot key registered by the RegisterHotKey function. The message is placed at the top of the message queue associated with the thread that registered the hot key.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_ICONERASEBKGND
member.summary: This message is sent to a minimized window when the background of the icon must be filled before painting the icon. A window receives this message only if a class icon is defined for the window; otherwise, WM_ERASEBKGND is sent.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_CHAR
member.summary: Sent to an application when the IME gets a character of the conversion result.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_COMPOSITION
member.summary: Sent to an application when the IME changes composition status as a result of a keystroke. A window receives this message through its WindowProc function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_COMPOSITIONFULL
member.summary: Sent to an application when the IME window finds no space to extend the area for the composition window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_CONTROL
member.summary: Sent by an application to direct the IME window to carry out the requested command. The application uses this message to control the IME window that it has created. To send this message, the application calls the SendMessage function with the following parameters.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_ENDCOMPOSITION
member.summary: Sent to an application when the IME ends composition. A window receives this message through its WindowProc function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_KEYDOWN
member.summary: Sent to an application by the IME to notify the application of a key press and to keep message order.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_KEYLAST
member.summary: Sent to an application by the IME to notify the application of a key last and to keep message order.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_KEYUP
member.summary: Sent to an application by the IME to notify the application of a key release and to keep message order

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_NOTIFY
member.summary: Sent to an application to notify it of changes to the IME window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_SELECT
member.summary: Sent to an application when the operating system is about to change the current IME.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_SETCONTEXT
member.summary: Sent to an application when a window is activated.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_IME_STARTCOMPOSITION
member.summary: Sent immediately before the IME generates the composition string as a result of a keystroke.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_INITDIALOG
member.summary: Sent to the dialog box procedure immediately before a dialog box is displayed. Dialog box procedures typically use this message to initialize controls and carry out any other initialization tasks that affect the appearance of the dialog box.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_INITMENU
member.summary: Sent when a menu is about to become active. It occurs when the user clicks an item on the menu bar or presses a menu key. This allows the application to modify the menu before it is displayed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_INITMENUPOPUP
member.summary: Sent when a drop-down menu or submenu is about to become active. This allows an application to modify the menu before it is displayed, without changing the entire menu.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE
member.summary: Sent to the topmost affected window after an application's input language has been changed. You should make any application-specific settings and pass the message to the DefWindowProc function, which passes the message to all first-level child windows. These child windows can pass the message to DefWindowProc to have it pass the message to their child windows, and so on.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_INPUTLANGCHANGEREQUEST
member.summary: Posted to the window with the focus when the user chooses a new input language, either with the hotkey (specified in the Keyboard control panel application) or from the indicator on the system taskbar. An application can accept the change by passing the message to the DefWindowProc function or reject the change (and prevent it from taking place) by returning immediately.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_KEYDOWN
member.summary: Posted to the window with the keyboard focus when a nonsystem key is pressed. A nonsystem key is a key that is pressed when the ALT key is not pressed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_KEYFIRST
member.summary: This message filters for keyboard messages.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_KEYLAST
member.summary: This message filters for keyboard messages.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_KEYUP
member.summary: Posted to the window with the keyboard focus when a nonsystem key is released. A nonsystem key is a key that is pressed when the ALT key is not pressed, or a keyboard key that is pressed when a window has the keyboard focus.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_KILLFOCUS
member.summary: Sent to a window immediately before it loses the keyboard focus.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK
member.summary: Posted when the user double-clicks the left mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_LBUTTONDOWN
member.summary: Posted when the user presses the left mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_LBUTTONUP
member.summary: Posted when the user releases the left mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MBUTTONDBLCLK
member.summary: Posted when the user double-clicks the middle mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MBUTTONDOWN
member.summary: Posted when the user presses the middle mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MBUTTONUP
member.summary: Posted when the user releases the middle mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDIACTIVATE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDIACTIVATE message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to instruct the client window to activate a different MDI child window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDICASCADE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDICASCADE message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to arrange all its child windows in a cascade format.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDICREATE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDICREATE message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to create an MDI child window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDIDESTROY
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDIDESTROY message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to close an MDI child window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDIGETACTIVE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDIGETACTIVE message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to retrieve the handle to the active MDI child window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDIICONARRANGE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDIICONARRANGE message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to arrange all minimized MDI child windows. It does not affect child windows that are not minimized.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDIMAXIMIZE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDIMAXIMIZE message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to maximize an MDI child window. The system resizes the child window to make its client area fill the client window. The system places the child window's window menu icon in the rightmost position of the frame window's menu bar, and places the child window's restore icon in the leftmost position. The system also appends the title bar text of the child window to that of the frame window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDINEXT
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDINEXT message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to activate the next or previous child window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDIREFRESHMENU
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDIREFRESHMENU message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to refresh the window menu of the MDI frame window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDIRESTORE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDIRESTORE message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to restore an MDI child window from maximized or minimized size.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDISETMENU
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDISETMENU message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to replace the entire menu of an MDI frame window, to replace the window menu of the frame window, or both.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MDITILE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_MDITILE message to a multiple-document interface (MDI) client window to arrange all of its MDI child windows in a tile format.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MEASUREITEM
member.summary: Sent to the owner window of a combo box, list box, list-view control, or menu item when the control or menu is created.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MENUCHAR
member.summary: Sent when a menu is active and the user presses a key that does not correspond to any mnemonic or accelerator key. This message is sent to the window that owns the menu.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MENUSELECT
member.summary: Sent to a menu's owner window when the user selects a menu item.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOUSEACTIVATE
member.summary: Sent when the cursor is in an inactive window and the user presses a mouse button. The parent window receives this message only if the child window passes it to the DefWindowProc function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOUSEFIRST
member.summary: Specify the first mouse message.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOUSEHOVER
member.summary: Posted to a window when the cursor hovers over the client area of the window for the period of time specified in a prior call to TrackMouseEvent.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOUSELAST
member.summary: Posted to a window to get the last mouse position.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOUSELEAVE
member.summary: Posted to a window when the cursor leaves the client area of the window specified in a prior call to TrackMouseEvent.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOUSEMOVE
member.summary: Posted to a window when the cursor moves. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOUSEWHEEL
member.summary: Sent to the focus window when the mouse wheel is rotated. The DefWindowProc function propagates the message to the window's parent. There should be no internal forwarding of the message, since DefWindowProc propagates it up the parent chain until it finds a window that processes it.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOVE
member.summary: Sent after a window has been moved.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_MOVING
member.summary: Sent while window is in moving.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCACTIVATE
member.summary: Sent to a window when its non client area needs to be changed to indicate an active or inactive state.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCCALCSIZE
member.summary: Sent when the size and position of a window's client area must be calculated. By processing this message, an application can control the content of the window's client area when the size or position of the window changes.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCCREATE
member.summary: Sent prior to the WM_CREATE message when a window is first created.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCDESTROY
member.summary: Notifies a window that its non client area is being destroyed. The DestroyWindow function sends the WM_NCDESTROY message to the window following the WM_DESTROY message.WM_DESTROY is used to free the allocated memory object associated with the window. The WM_NCDESTROY message is sent after the child windows have been destroyed. In contrast, WM_DESTROY is sent before the child windows are destroyed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCHITTEST
member.summary: Sent to a window in order to determine what part of the window corresponds to a particular screen coordinate. This can happen, for example, when the cursor moves, when a mouse button is pressed or released, or in response to a call to a function such as WindowFromPoint. If the mouse is not captured, the message is sent to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is sent to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCLBUTTONDBLCLK
member.summary: Posted when the user double-clicks the left mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCLBUTTONDOWN
member.summary: Posted when the user presses the left mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCLBUTTONUP
member.summary: Posted when the user releases the left mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCMBUTTONDBLCLK
member.summary: Posted when the user double-clicks the middle mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCMBUTTONDOWN
member.summary: Posted when the user presses the middle mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCMBUTTONUP
member.summary: Posted when the user releases the middle mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCMOUSEHOVER
member.summary: Posted to a window when the cursor hovers over the non-client area of the window for the period of time specified in a prior call to TrackMouseEvent.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCMOUSELEAVE
member.summary: Posted to a window when the cursor leaves the non-client area of the window specified in a prior call to TrackMouseEvent.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCMOUSEMOVE
member.summary: Posted to a window when the cursor is moved within the non-client area of the window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCRBUTTONDBLCLK
member.summary: Posted when the user double-clicks the right mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCRBUTTONDOWN
member.summary: Posted when the user presses the right mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NCRBUTTONUP
member.summary: Posted when the user releases the right mouse button while the cursor is within the non-client area of a window. This message is posted to the window that contains the cursor. If a window has captured the mouse, this message is not posted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NEXTDLGCTL
member.summary: Sent to a dialog box procedure to set the keyboard focus to a different control in the dialog box.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NEXTMENU
member.summary: Sent to an application when the right or left arrow key is used to switch between the menu bar and the system menu.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NOTIFY
member.summary: Sent by a common control to its parent window when an event has occurred or the control requires some information.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NOTIFYFORMAT
member.summary: Determines if a window accepts ANSI or Unicode structures in the WM_NOTIFY notification message. WM_NOTIFYFORMAT messages are sent from a common control to its parent window and from the parent window to the common control.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_NULL
member.summary: Performs no operation. An application sends the WM_NULL message if it wants to post a message that the recipient window will ignore.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PALETTECHANGED
member.summary: The WM_PALETTECHANGED message is sent to all top-level and overlapped windows after the window with the keyboard focus has realized its logical palette, thereby changing the system palette. This message enables a window that uses a color palette but does not have the keyboard focus to realize its logical palette and update its client area.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PALETTEISCHANGING
member.summary: The WM_PALETTEISCHANGING message informs applications that an application is going to realize its logical palette.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PARENTNOTIFY
member.summary: Sent to a window when a significant action occurs on a descendant window. This message is now extended to include the WM_POINTERDOWN event. When the child window is being created, the system sends WM_PARENTNOTIFY just before the CreateWindow or CreateWindowEx function that creates the window returns. When the child window is being destroyed, the system sends the message before any processing to destroy the window takes place.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PASTE
member.summary: An application sends a WM_PASTE message to an edit control or combo box to copy the current content of the clipboard to the edit control at the current caret position. Data is inserted only if the clipboard contains data in CF_TEXT format.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PENWINFIRST
member.summary: The pend that creates first for the drawing.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PENWINLAST
member.summary: The pend that creates last for the drawing.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_POWER
member.summary: Notifies applications that the system, typically a battery-powered personal computer, is about to enter a suspended mode.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_POWERBROADCAST
member.summary: Notifies applications that a power-management event has occurred.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PRINT
member.summary: The WM_PRINT message is sent to a window to request that it draw itself in the specified device context, most commonly in a printer device context.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PRINTCLIENT
member.summary: The WM_PRINTCLIENT message is sent to a window to request that it draw its client area in the specified device context, most commonly in a printer device context. Unlike WM_PRINT, WM_PRINTCLIENT is not processed by DefWindowProc. A window should process the WM_PRINTCLIENT message through an application-defined WindowProc function for it to be used properly.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PSD_ENVSTAMPRECT
member.summary: Notifies the hook procedure of a Page Setup dialog box, PagePaintHook, that the dialog box is about to draw the envelope-stamp rectangle of the sample page.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PSD_FULLPAGERECT
member.summary: Notifies a PagePaintHook hook procedure of the coordinates of the sample page rectangle in the Page Setup dialog box. The dialog box sends this message when it is about to draw the contents of the sample page.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PSD_GREEKTEXTRECT
member.summary: Notifies the hook procedure of a Page Setup dialog box, PagePaintHook, that the dialog box is about to draw Greek text inside the margin rectangle of the sample page.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PSD_MARGINRECT
member.summary: Notifies the hook procedure of a Page Setup dialog box, PagePaintHook, that the dialog box is about to draw the margin rectangle of the sample page.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PSD_MINMARGINRECT
member.summary: Notifies a PagePaintHook hook procedure of the coordinates of the margin rectangle in the sample page. A Page Setup dialog box sends this message when it is about to draw the contents of the sample page.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PSD_PAGESETUPDLG
member.summary: Notifies a PagePaintHook hook procedure that the Page Setup dialog box is about to draw the contents of the sample page. The hook procedure can use this message to carry out initialization tasks related to drawing the contents of the sample page.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_PSD_YAFULLPAGERECT
member.summary: Notifies the hook procedure of a Page Setup dialog box, PagePaintHook, that the dialog box is about to draw the return address portion of an envelope sample page.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_QUERYDRAGICON
member.summary: Sent to a minimized (iconic) window. The window is about to be dragged by the user but does not have an icon defined for its class. An application can return a handle to an icon or cursor. The system displays this cursor or icon while the user drags the icon.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_QUERYENDSESSION
member.summary: The WM_QUERYENDSESSION message is sent when the user chooses to end the session or when an application calls one of the system shutdown functions. If any application returns zero, the session is not ended. The system stops sending WM_QUERYENDSESSION messages as soon as one application returns zero. After processing this message, the system sends the WM_ENDSESSION message with the wParam parameter set to the results of the WM_QUERYENDSESSION message.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_QUERYNEWPALETTE
member.summary: The WM_QUERYNEWPALETTE message informs a window that it is about to receive the keyboard focus, giving the window the opportunity to realize its logical palette when it receives the focus.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_QUERYOPEN
member.summary: Sent to an icon when the user requests that the window be restored to its previous size and position.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_QUERYUISTATE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_QUERYUISTATE message to retrieve the UI state for a window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_QUEUESYNC
member.summary: Sent by a computer-based training (CBT) application to separate user-input messages from other messages sent through the WH_JOURNALPLAYBACK procedure.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_QUIT
member.summary: Indicates a request to terminate an application, and is generated when the application calls the PostQuitMessage function. This message causes the GetMessage function to return zero.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_RBUTTONDBLCLK
member.summary: Posted when the user double-clicks the right mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_RBUTTONDOWN
member.summary: Posted when the user presses the right mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_RBUTTONUP
member.summary: Posted when the user releases the right mouse button while the cursor is in the client area of a window. If the mouse is not captured, the message is posted to the window beneath the cursor. Otherwise, the message is posted to the window that has captured the mouse.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_RENDERALLFORMATS
member.summary: Sent to the clipboard owner before it is destroyed, if the clipboard owner has delayed rendering one or more clipboard formats. For the content of the clipboard to remain available to other applications, the clipboard owner must render data in all the formats it is capable of generating, and place the data on the clipboard by calling the SetClipboardData function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_RENDERFORMAT
member.summary: Sent to the clipboard owner if it has delayed rendering a specific clipboard format and if an application has requested data in that format. The clipboard owner must render data in the specified format and place it on the clipboard by calling the SetClipboardData function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SETCURSOR
member.summary: Sent to a window if the mouse causes the cursor to move within a window and mouse input is not captured.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SETFOCUS
member.summary: Sent to a window after it has gained the keyboard focus.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SETFONT
member.summary: Sets the font that a control is to use when drawing text.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SETHOTKEY
member.summary: Sent to a window to associate a hot key with the window. When the user presses the hot key, the system activates the window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SETICON
member.summary: Associates a new large or small icon with a window. The system displays the large icon in the ALT+TAB dialog box, and the small icon in the window caption.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SETTEXT
member.summary: Sets the text of a window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SETTINGCHANGE
member.summary: A message that is sent to all top-level windows when the SystemParametersInfo function changes a system-wide setting or when policy settings have changed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SHOWWINDOW
member.summary: Sent to a window when the window is about to be hidden or shown.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SIZE
member.summary: Sent to a window after its size has changed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SIZECLIPBOARD
member.summary: Sent to the clipboard owner by a clipboard viewer window when the clipboard contains data in the CF_OWNERDISPLAY format and the clipboard viewer's client area has changed size.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SIZING
member.summary: Sent to a window that the user is resizing. By processing this message, an application can monitor the size and position of the drag rectangle and, if needed, change its size or position.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SPOOLERSTATUS
member.summary: The WM_SPOOLERSTATUS message is sent from Print Manager whenever a job is added to or removed from the Print Manager queue.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_STYLECHANGED
member.summary: Sent to a window after the SetWindowLong function has changed one or more of the window's styles.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_STYLECHANGING
member.summary: Sent to a window when the SetWindowLong function is about to change one or more of the window's styles.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SYSCHAR
member.summary: Posted to the window with the keyboard focus when a WM_SYSKEYDOWN message is translated by the TranslateMessage function. It specifies the character code of a system character key — that is, a character key that is pressed while the ALT key is down.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SYSCOLORCHANGE
member.summary: The WM_SYSCOLORCHANGE message is sent to all top-level windows when a change is made to a system color setting.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SYSCOMMAND
member.summary: A window receives this message when the user chooses a command from the Window menu (formerly known as the system or control menu) or when the user chooses the maximize button, minimize button, restore button, or close button.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SYSDEADCHAR
member.summary: Sent to the window with the keyboard focus when a WM_SYSKEYDOWN message is translated by the TranslateMessage function. WM_SYSDEADCHAR specifies the character code of a system dead key — that is, a dead key that is pressed while holding down the ALT key.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SYSKEYDOWN
member.summary: Posted to the window with the keyboard focus when the user presses the F10 key (which activates the menu bar) or holds down the ALT key and then presses another key. It also occurs when no window currently has the keyboard focus; in this case, the WM_SYSKEYDOWN message is sent to the active window. The window that receives the message can distinguish between these two contexts by checking the context code in the lParam parameter.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_SYSKEYUP
member.summary: Posted to the window with the keyboard focus when the user releases a key that was pressed while the ALT key was held down. It also occurs when no window currently has the keyboard focus; in this case, the WM_SYSKEYUP message is sent to the active window. The window that receives the message can distinguish between these two contexts by checking the context code in the lParam parameter.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_TCARD
member.summary: Sent to an application that has initiated a training card with Windows Help. The message informs the application when the user clicks an authorable button. An application initiates a training card by specifying the HELP_TCARD command in a call to the WinHelp function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_TIMECHANGE
member.summary: A message that is sent whenever there is a change in the system time.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_TIMER
member.summary: Posted to the installing thread's message queue when a timer expires. The message is posted by the GetMessage or PeekMessage function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_UNDO
member.summary: An application sends a WM_UNDO message to an edit control to undo the last operation. When this message is sent to an edit control, the previously deleted text is restored or the previously added text is deleted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_UPDATEUISTATE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_UPDATEUISTATE message to change the UI state for the specified window and all its child windows.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_USER
member.summary: Used to define private messages for use by private window classes, usually of the form WM_USER+x, where x is an integer value.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_USERCHANGED
member.summary: Sent to all windows after the user has logged on or off. When the user logs on or off, the system updates the user-specific settings. The system sends this message immediately after updating the settings.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_VKEYTOITEM
member.summary: Sent by a list box with the LBS_WANTKEYBOARDINPUT style to its owner in response to a WM_KEYDOWN message.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGED
member.summary: Sent to a window whose size, position, or place in the Z order has changed as a result of a call to the SetWindowPos function or another window-management function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING
member.summary: Sent to a window whose size, position, or place in the Z order is about to change as a result of a call to the SetWindowPos function or another window-management function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WM_WININICHANGE
member.summary: An application sends the WM_WININICHANGE message to all top-level windows after making a change to the WIN.INI file. The SystemParametersInfo function sends this message after an application uses the function to change a setting in WIN.INI.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_OVERLAPPED
member.summary: The window is an overlapped window. An overlapped window has a title bar and a border. Same as the WS_TILED style.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_POPUP
member.summary: The windows is a pop-up window. This style cannot be used with the WS_CHILD style.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_CHILD
member.summary: The window is a child window. A window with this style cannot have a menu bar. This style cannot be used with the WS_POPUP style.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_MINIMIZE
member.summary: The window is initially minimized. Same as the WS_ICONIC style.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_VISIBLE
member.summary: The window is initially visible. This style can be turned on and off by using the ShowWindow or SetWindowPos function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_DISABLED
member.summary: The window is initially disabled. A disabled window cannot receive input from the user. To change this after a window has been created, use the EnableWindow function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_CLIPSIBLINGS
member.summary: Clips child windows relative to each other; that is, when a particular child window receives a WM_PAINT message, the WS_CLIPSIBLINGS style clips all other overlapping child windows out of the region of the child window to be updated. If WS_CLIPSIBLINGS is not specified and child windows overlap, it is possible, when drawing within the client area of a child window, to draw within the client area of a neighboring child window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_CLIPCHILDREN
member.summary: Excludes the area occupied by child windows when drawing occurs within the parent window. This style is used when creating the parent window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_MAXIMIZE
member.summary: The window is initially maximized.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_CAPTION
member.summary: The window has a title bar (includes the WS_BORDER style).

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_BORDER
member.summary: The window has a thin-line border.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_DLGFRAME
member.summary: The window has a border of a style typically used with dialog boxes. A window with this style cannot have a title bar.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_VSCROLL
member.summary: The window has a vertical scroll bar.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_HSCROLL
member.summary: The window has a horizontal scroll bar.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_SYSMENU
member.summary: The window has a window menu on its title bar. The WS_CAPTION style must also be specified.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_THICKFRAME
member.summary: The window has a sizing border. Same as the WS_SIZEBOX style.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_TABSTOP
member.summary: The window is a control that can receive the keyboard focus when the user presses the TAB key. Pressing the TAB key changes the keyboard focus to the next control with the WS_TABSTOP style.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_MINIMIZEBOX
member.summary: The window has a minimize button. Cannot be combined with the WS_EX_CONTEXTHELP style. The WS_SYSMENU style must also be specified.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_MAXIMIZEBOX
member.summary: The window has a maximize button. Cannot be combined with the WS_EX_CONTEXTHELP style. The WS_SYSMENU style must also be specified.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_DLGMODALFRAME
member.summary: The window has a double border; the window can, optionally, be created with a title bar by specifying the WS_CAPTION style in the dwStyle parameter.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_MDICHILD
member.summary: The window is a MDI child window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW
member.summary: The window is intended to be used as a floating toolbar. A tool window has a title bar that is shorter than a normal title bar, and the window title is drawn using a smaller font. A tool window does not appear in the taskbar or in the dialog that appears when the user presses ALT+TAB. If a tool window has a system menu, its icon is not displayed on the title bar. However, you can display the system menu by right-clicking or by typing ALT+SPACE.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_CLIENTEDGE
member.summary: The window has a border with a sunken edge.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_CONTEXTHELP
member.summary: The title bar of the window includes a question mark. When the user clicks the question mark, the cursor changes to a question mark with a pointer. If the user then clicks a child window, the child receives a WM_HELP message. The child window should pass the message to the parent window procedure, which should call the WinHelp function using the HELP_WM_HELP command. The Help application displays a pop-up window that typically contains help for the child window. WS_EX_CONTEXTHELP cannot be used with the WS_MAXIMIZEBOX or WS_MINIMIZEBOX styles.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_RIGHT
member.summary: The window has generic "right-aligned" properties. This depends on the window class. This style has an effect only if the shell language is Hebrew, Arabic, or another language that supports reading-order alignment; otherwise, the style is ignored.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_LEFT
member.summary: The window has generic left-aligned properties. This is the default.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_RTLREADING
member.summary: If the shell language is Hebrew, Arabic, or another language that supports reading-order alignment, the window text is displayed using right-to-left reading-order properties. For other languages, the style is ignored.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_LEFTSCROLLBAR
member.summary: If the shell language is Hebrew, Arabic, or another language that supports reading order alignment, the vertical scroll bar (if present) is to the left of the client area. For other languages, the style is ignored.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_CONTROLPARENT
member.summary: The window itself contains child windows that should take part in dialog box navigation. If this style is specified, the dialog manager recursive into children of this window when performing navigation operations such as handling the TAB key, an arrow key, or a keyboard mnemonic.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_STATICEDGE
member.summary: The window has a three-dimensional border style intended to be used for items that do not accept user input.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_APPWINDOW
member.summary: Forces a top-level window onto the task-bar when the window is visible.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_LAYERED
member.summary: The window is a layered window. This style cannot be used if the window has a class style of either CS_OWNDC or CS_CLASSDC.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_TOPMOST
member.summary: The window should be placed above all non-topmost windows and should stay above them, even when the window is deactivated. To add or remove this style, use the SetWindowPos function.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_WINDOWEDGE
member.summary: The window has a border with a raised edge.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_NOINHERITLAYOUT
member.summary: The window has a border with a raised edge.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.WS_EX_LAYOUTRTL
member.summary: If the shell language is Hebrew, Arabic, or another language that supports reading order alignment, the horizontal origin of the window is on the right edge. Increasing horizontal values advance to the left.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_SIZE
member.summary: Sizes the window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_MOVE
member.summary: Moves the window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_MINIMIZE
member.summary: Minimizes the window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_MAXIMIZE
member.summary: Maximizes the window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_CLOSE
member.summary: Closes the window.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_MOUSEMENU
member.summary: Retrieves the window menu as a result of a mouse click.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_KEYMENU
member.summary: Retrieves the window menu as a result of a keystroke. For more information, see the Remarks section.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_RESTORE
member.summary: Restores the window to its normal position and size.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.WinForms.Core.WindowMessages.SC_CONTEXTHELP

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Drawing.AnimationHelper
member.summary: Utility class comes handy when you need to perform simple animations in your control.

remarks.para: The method in this class allows you to specify the number of animation positions (0 to N), the direction of animation (whether animation is from 0 towards N or from N towards 0), and the speed (X) at which animation is performed.

When the method is called, the current animation position is set ( property) which gets reduced (or incremented based on the direction of animation) every X time interval specified in the method call, until it reaches the other extreme of the Animation position range. Every time the value changes, an event is thrown. Upon reaching the last animation position, an event is thrown.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Drawing.BrushInfo
member.summary: Holds information on how to fill the background of a window or grid cell.
member.remarks:
BrushInfo lets you specify a solid backcolor, gradient or pattern style with both back and forecolor.
This information can be persisted with serialization.
You can also convert the information to a string and recreate it from a string.
BrushInfo is immutable (just like ). You cannot change its values. Instead you have to create a new BrushInfo object.
BrushInfo can also be persisted into code when used as a property in a component designer.
shows how to fill a rectangle using information.

member.summary: Draws an image using the ImageList, taking into account the Graphics.ClipBounds.
member.param: The Graphics object into which to draw.
The rectangle into which to draw.
member.remarks:
This method will use ImageList_DrawEx to draw the image (to use the transparency info in the embedded images). We use the PInvoke rather than ImageList.Draw because, the Draw method uses the PaintEventArgs.ClipRectangle rather than g.ClipBounds (both can be different) and here we force the ClipBounds on the DC.
Also, you do not have to use this method if your images will never be drawn clipped (in that case just use ImageList.Draw).

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Runtime.Serialization.AppStateSerializer
member.summary: Provides a mechanism for coordinating the serialization behavior of multiple components.

remarks.para: The AppStateSerializer class is a serialization utility that allows multiple components in an application to access a common disk I/O medium for state persistence. Using the same storage medium for persisting the state information across components, without overtly tying them together, helps avoid the file clutter that is bound to occur by components using distinct files. Though primarily developed for use by Syncfusion products, the AppStateSerializer is generic enough to be availed of by other components as well.

The AppStateSerializer supports serializing into the system's Isolated Storage, Windows Registry, an XML file, a binary file or to an externally provided Stream. Take a look at the enumeration for more information on these different supported modes.
To use the services of this class, you can create a new instance or use the global Singleton instance. These two usage patterns are explained below:

1) Using the Singleton: The AppStateSerializer class provides you a singleton instance (through the ) using which you can persist all your app. info into a single medium. This singleton, by default, is configured to persist in the Isolated Storage (with the scope IsolatedStorageScope.Assembly|IsolatedStorageScope.Domain|IsolatedStorageScope.User). This usage pattern is akin to creating an instance of this class and using the same instance to persist all your app information. But, note that this Singleton is also used by the Controls and Components in Essential Tools to persist their information. The default Storage medium of this Singleton instance can also be customized using the static method. In short, use the Singleton whenever you want all your persistence information to be stored in a single medium (along with the persistence information of the Controls and Components in Essential Tools).

2) Using an instance: As an alternative you could create a custom instance of this class, configuring it to use one of the above storage mediums and persist one or more information into it. You can use this in tandem with the above Singleton instance if you wish. Make sure to call method when you are done writing into the serializer.
In both the above cases use the method's and to persist or depersist from the storage medium set for that instance.

Note that the AppStateSerializer class uses "Simple" type names (not strongly typed) to serialize types. This is necessary to enable usage of persisted information across different but compatible versions of an assembly. This will however cause the deserialization process to convert the serialized data to the type from the latest version of the assembly installed in the GAC, instead of the version that your app is linking to. You can overcome this by using the method.

remarks.para: The AppStateSerializer class, by default, uses "Simple" assembly names (not strongly typed) to serialize types. This renders the deserialization process unpredictable because the resultant type of an object after deserialization is dependent upon the latest version of that assembly installed in the GAC, if any. member.name: T:Syncfusion.Styles.StyleInfoBase
member.summary:
Provides a wrapper object for the object with type safe access to all properties stored in the style object.
Style objects provide a very user friendly way to modify data. It is very much like in Excel VBA. For example, to change the bold setting for a cell, you simply call grid[5,2].Font.Bold = True.
member.remarks:
The is a wrapper around the . It provides type safe accessor properties to modify data of the underlying data store and can hold temporary information about the style object that does not need to be persisted.
In Essential Grid for the example, the GridStyleInfo class holds extensive identity information about a style object such as cached base styles, row and column index, a reference to the grid model, and more. This is all the information that can be discarded when the style is no longer used (because maybe the cell is not visible anymore). Only the part needs to be kept alive.
Style objects only exist temporarily and will be created as a weak reference in a volatile data store. Once Garbage Collection kicks in smart style objects that are not referenced any more will be garbage collected. The volatile data cache can also be cleared manually.
Because Style objects know their identity they can notify their owner of changes or load base style information when the user interacts with the style object. This allows you to make changes to a style object directly, such as Cell.Font.Bold = True;
Style objects support property inheritance from parent styles, e.g. in a grid a cell can inherit properties from a parent row, column, table or a collection of names styles in a base styles map.
Style objects support subobjects. Subobjects can support inheritance (e.g. a Font.Bold can be inherited). Immutable subobjects like BrushInfo don't support inheritance of individual properties.
allows you to register any number of properties but keeps the data very memory efficient. Only properties that are actually used for a style object will be allocated for an object. The StyleObjectStore handles the storage of the object. For short integers, enums and Boolean values, the data will be stored in a BitVector32 structure to save even more memory.
Programmers can derive their own style classes from and add type-safe (and intellisense) supported custom properties to the style class. If you write, for example, your own SpinButton class that needs individual properties, simply add a �CellSpinButtonInfo� class as subobject. If you derive CellSpinButtonInfo from StyleInfoSubObjectBase, your new object will support property inheritance from base styles.
Style objects can be written into a string (see ) and later be recreated using the method. When writing the string you have the option to show default values (use the �d� format). Subobjects will be identified with a dot �.�, e.g. �Font.Bold�
Style object support several operations how to combine information from two styles. Style operations include: apply changes, apply initialized properties, override initialized properties, exclude properties. See the method.
Style objects integrate with . The property grid displays values that belong to a style object in bold. Values that are inherited from parent styles will be displayed as default values. The user can select several cells in a grid and the operation will show common settings in the property grid as bold.
Style objects support BeginUpdate, EndUpdate mechanism. This allows users to batch several operations on a style object into one transaction.
member.example:
The following example shows how you can use the GridFontInfo class in Essential Grid:
standard.Font.Facename = "Helvetica"; model[1, 3].Font.Bold = true; string faceName = model[1, 3].Font.Facename; // any cell inherits standard style Console.WriteLIne(faceName); // will output "Helvetica" Console.WriteLIne(model[1, 3].Font.Bold); // will output "true" Console.WriteLIne(model[1, 3].Font.HasFaceName); // will output "False"

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Styles.StyleInfoStore
member.summary: Provides storage for the object.
member.remarks:
You cannot instantiate a class directly. You have to derive a concrete class from this class that you can instantiate.
In derived classes of , you always need to implement a / pair. The holds all the data that are specific to the style object and should be persisted.
The is a wrapper around the . It provides type safe accessor properties to modify data of the underlying data store and can hold temporary information about the style object that does not need to be persisted.
In Essential Grid for example, the GridStyleInfo class holds extensive identity information about a style object such as cached base styles, row and column index, a reference to the grid model and more. These are all the information that can be discarded when the style is no longer used (because maybe the cell is not visible anymore). Only the part needs to be kept alive.
allows you to register any number of properties but keeps the data very memory efficient. Only properties that are actually used for a style object will be allocated for an object. The StyleObjectStore handles the storage of objects. For short integers, enums and Boolean values the data will be stored in a BitVector32 structure to save even more memory.
See the overview for for further discussion about style objects.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Styles.StyleInfoSubObjectBase
member.summary: is an abstract base class for classes to be used as subobjects in a .
member.remarks:
is derived from and thus provides the same easy way to provide properties that can inherit values from base styles at run-time.
The difference is that supports this inheritance mechanism as a subobject from a . A subobject needs to have knowledge about its parent object and be able to walk the base styles from the parent object.
Examples for implementation of are the font and border classes in Essential Grid.
Programmers can derive their own style classes from and add type-safe (and Intelli-sense) supported custom properties to the style class. If you write your own SpinButton class that needs individual properties, simply add a "CellSpinButtonInfo" class as subobject. If you derive CellSpinButtonInfo from StyleInfoSubObjectBase, your new object will support property inheritance from base styles.
See the overview for for further discussion about style objects.
member.example:
The following example shows how you can use the GridFontInfo class in Essential Grid:
standard.Font.Facename = "Helvetica"; model[1, 3].Font.Bold = true; string faceName = model[1, 3].Font.Facename; // any cell inherits standard style Console.WriteLIne(faceName); // will output "Helvetica" Console.WriteLIne(model[1, 3].Font.Bold); // will output "true" Console.WriteLIne(model[1, 3].Font.HasFaceName); // will output "False"
